sources.entry: LockPlus - WireGuard and OpenVPN client with a kill switch that macOS itself enforces. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/steiale/lockplus) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: LockPlus is a native macOS menu-bar VPN client for WireGuard and OpenVPN whose kill switch is enforced by macOS itself (includeAllNetworks), running tunnels in a system extension with no root helper.
keywords: stop internet leaks when vpn drops
summary.what_it_does: LockPlus imports WireGuard (.conf) and OpenVPN (.ovpn, zip) profiles, with a report checking each OpenVPN directive before saving. It connects using wireguard-go for WireGuard and OpenVPN 3 for OpenVPN, both inside a macOS system extension. OpenVPN supports password, static challenge, and dynamic challenge/response (CRV1) sign-in, including a new code on reconnect. The kill switch blocks traffic outside the tunnel, including during reconnects, with an optional "Allow local network" exception; split-tunnel profiles get route protection instead. It can auto-connect on untrusted Wi-Fi or Ethernet via macOS on-demand rules, pause protection for a set time, and verify DNS through the tunnel. The README also describes diagnostics and logs with secrets removed, and migration of profiles and settings from LockPlus 1.x.
use_cases: keep all Mac traffic inside a WireGuard or OpenVPN tunnel
connect to a work OpenVPN server that uses one-time codes
auto-connect VPN on untrusted Wi-Fi networks
stop traffic leaking when the VPN drops
import an existing WireGuard or OpenVPN config into a Mac app
pause VPN for a captive-portal hotel or café login
how_to_run: Download LockPlus.dmg from the releases and drag LockPlus to Applications
On first launch, approve the LockPlus system extension and VPN configuration in System Settings
Build from source: native/Tools/bootstrap/vendor.sh and openssl.sh fetch and build pinned dependencies
Run native/Tools/dev/build.sh to build a development version
notable: Kill switch enforced by macOS via includeAllNetworks rather than pf firewall rules
No root helper or administrator prompt to connect; tunnel runs in a system extension approved once
OpenVPN dynamic challenge/response (CRV1) and one-time-code sign-in
Import report that marks each OpenVPN directive as supported, not needed, not applied, or not supported
Built with AI coding agents; two separate AI review engines reviewed security changes, with reports published in docs/reviews/
caveats: Requires macOS 26 or later and Apple silicon; Intel is not supported
One active tunnel at a time; profile switching leaves a brief unprotected moment
OpenVPN: no TAP, plugins, or SSO sign-in; BF-CBC, DES, 3DES and auth MD5 unsupported
Kill switch has a brief under-2-second gap if the tunnel process crashes; no independent human security audit yet
